trust_decision.summary: Untrusted URI strings and port strings are validated by anchored regexes whose leading whitespace run overlaps the following quantifier, so a long whitespace run followed by an invalid char backtracks quadratically; the fix makes the leading whitespace quantifier possessive.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'URI gem ReDoS', and the default URI.parse/URI.split go through RFC3986_PARSER (lib/uri/common.rb:151, lib/uri/common.rb:188), so an engineer greps the RFC3986 parser regexes first and finds the PORT regex with adjacent whitespace/digit quantifiers.

fix_sites.entry_point: URI::Generic#port= on a URI from URI.parse (RFC3986_PARSER) via check_port, lib/uri/generic.rb:719-721 -> lib/uri/generic.rb:679; also Generic.new(..., RFC3986_PARSER, true) via lib/uri/generic.rb:191

URI::RFC2396_Parser#split / #parse (lib/uri/rfc2396_parser.rb:120-150, lib/uri/rfc2396_parser.rb:209-211), i.e. URI::Parser.new / URI::DEFAULT_PARSER (lib/uri/common.rb:17, lib/uri/common.rb:22); also Generic#coerce when the object's parser is DEFAULT_PARSER (lib/uri/generic.rb:1466, lib/uri/generic.rb:289-294)
fix_sites.module_kind: second (legacy RFC2396) parser implementation, regex builder

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/uri/rfc2396_parser.rb:500-501 (legacy RFC2396 parser; default URI.parse uses RFC3986_PARSER at lib/uri/common.rb:188)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: URI.parse/URI.split use the RFC3986 parser, so the RFC2396 parser looks like a legacy class only reached by explicit URI::Parser/DEFAULT_PARSER use or URI.extract, which is marked obsolete (lib/uri/common.rb:253).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Leading/trailing ASCII whitespace around a port string and around a whole URI given to RFC2396_Parser#split must still be accepted (the \s* wrappers exist for that); a fix that drops the whitespace allowance or rejects whitespace breaks valid inputs.

O6_input_shapes: port given as String (Integer ports skip the regex, lib/uri/generic.rb:679)
whole absolute URI string to RFC2396 split (ABS_URI)
relative URI string to RFC2396 split (REL_URI)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another component regex in the same default_regexp table with a whitespace-tolerant prefix like PORT's
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PORT is the only entry in the table that tolerates surrounding whitespace; a maintainer extending that tolerance to another component would copy its non-possessive form.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the extract/regexp builders wrapping X_ABS_URI/X_REL_URI with the same whitespace prefix
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: They are built from the same patterns, right next to the fixed lines.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333, quadratic backtracking in input-validation regex)

O10_build.toolchain: ruby + rake + test-unit (test/lib from ruby/ruby supplies assert_linear_performance)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make only the RFC3986 PORT whitespace quantifier possessive (or add an input length cap) and leave the RFC2396 ABS_URI/REL_URI wrappers alone.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/uri/mailto.rb:148 and lib/uri/mailto.rb:52 apply nested-quantifier regexes to opaque mailto parts; not this advisory's regexes, not analysed.
lib/uri/generic.rb:1558 scans no_proxy env with a regex; environment input, not this advisory.
